# lean-pkg new

scaffold a new Lean package (Challenge/Solution, comparator.json, claims, coverage, verify.sh) in a new directory and git init it; no registry, no network.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg new [--kind {paper,library}] [--stack NAME|current|none] [--dir DIR]
             [--module MOD] [--no-mathlib] [--author TEXT] [--license {Apache-2.0,MIT}]
             [--json] NAME
```

Write a minimal Lean 4 package that comparator-receipt, `receipt systemd`, gate and reuse lint accept unchanged (and page, for --kind library; a paper's coverage.yaml waits for the paper), then `git init` it. Nothing is committed, fetched or built; no registry is read or written. Next steps: docs/quickstart.md.

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | the package name: lower-case letters, digits, single hyphens (e.g. my-proof) |
| `--kind {paper,library}` | paper (default): the paper is the product; coverage.yaml stays incomplete until you name the paper and `formalization anchor` binds its posted version. library: the Lean package is the product; coverage.yaml lists the example as its main result. Choices: `paper`, `library`. |
| `--stack NAME\|current\|none` | pin lean-toolchain and the Mathlib require to a declared LTS stack and write `stack: NAME` into coverage.yaml (docs/stacks/); current: the newest declared stack whose window covers today; none: the newest pins, no key. Default: current for --kind paper (the newest pins when no stack is current), none for --kind library. An undeclared name exits 2 |
| `--dir DIR` | where to write it (default ./NAME); refused when it exists and is not empty |
| `--module MOD` | the library and namespace (default: NAME in CamelCase, my-proof -&gt; MyProof) |
| `--no-mathlib` | core Lean only: no Mathlib dependency (fast to build; comparator-receipt then needs COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_NO_MATHLIB=1) |
| `--author TEXT` | the CITATION.cff author (default: git config user.name) |
| `--license {Apache-2.0,MIT}` | the LICENSE written (default Apache-2.0); pass the same id to `update NAME --license-spdx`. Choices: `Apache-2.0`, `MIT`. |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `new NAME` | scaffold a minimal Lean 4 package in `./NAME` (or `--dir DIR`; refused when it exists and is not empty) and `git init` it, for the [quickstart](../quickstart.md): the [getting-started template](../getting-started.md#start-from-scratch) (`lean-toolchain`, `.gitignore`, `lakefile.toml`, `MOD.lean`, `MOD/Challenge.lean`, `MOD/Solution.lean`, `comparator.json`) plus `MOD/Axioms.lean` (`#print axioms`), `claims.yaml` (one reusable claim), `coverage.yaml` (below), `CITATION.cff` (the author is `--author`, else `git config user.name`; a name with no space prints a warning, since it looks like a handle), `LICENSE` with the same text in `LICENSES/<SPDX>.txt`, a `REUSE.toml` that puts every file, receipts and logs included, under that license (so `reuse lint`, which [`publish --dry-run`](publish.md) runs, passes), a `README.md` carrying the lean-pkg credit, and `verify.sh`, the lower-tier check whose log [`receipt systemd --run`](receipt-systemd.md) reads. The `lakefile.toml` names its library in `defaultTargets`, so a bare `lake build` builds it, and globs both `MOD` and `MOD.+`, so the root module `MOD.lean` (written empty, for the library's imports) is built and a Solution may import the library through it. Nothing is committed, fetched or built, and no registry is read or written. `--stack NAME` pins a declared [LTS stack](../stacks/README.md): its `lean-toolchain` and Mathlib tag, and `stack: NAME` in `coverage.yaml`, which [`doctor NAME`](doctor.md), [`verify`](verify.md) and `page` check against the committed pins; `--stack current` is the newest declared stack whose window covers today and `--stack none` the newest pins with no key. Without `--stack`, `--kind paper` takes the current stack (the newest pins, with a warning, when none is current) and `--kind library` the newest pins (libraries aimed at Mathlib follow its newest release; proposal 0004, open question 7): the newest stable Lean release lean-pkg ships in its table, with the matching Mathlib tag, and a release candidate only when no stable release is newer. The output names the pins, and says when they are a release candidate (`--json`: `release_candidate`). `new` reads no network. An undeclared stack exits 2, listing the declared ones. The stack's comparator tools are the ones its toolchain bundles, so the toolchain pin is theirs. `--kind paper` (the default) writes a `kind: paper` `coverage.yaml` that is incomplete on purpose: `manuscript.version: unposted` and `FILL-ME` markers, which [`coverage check`](coverage.md) and `page` refuse until you name the paper and its results; [`formalization anchor --write`](formalization.md) then binds the posted version (no manuscript is invented). `--kind library`: one main result naming the example claim, which `coverage check` accepts as written. `--no-mathlib`: core Lean only (`lean-pkg receipt comparator` then needs `COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_NO_MATHLIB=1`; `verify.sh` logs `mathlib-rev: none`, the receipt's explicit value for a package without Mathlib). The name: lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter; a library named like Lean's or a Mathlib dependency's root namespace is refused (exit 2) | `[--kind paper\|library] [--stack NAME\|current\|none] [--dir DIR] [--module MOD] [--no-mathlib] [--author TEXT] [--license Apache-2.0\|MIT] [--json]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `new-stack` (exit 0): `author`, `author_source`, `committed`, `coverage_complete`, `dir`, `files`, `git_init`, `kind`, `lean_toolchain`, `license_spdx`, `mathlib`, `mathlib_rev`, `module`, `name`, `next_commands`, `ok`, `registry_touched`, `release_candidate`, `stack`, `stack_source`, `warnings`

## Examples

Scaffold a companion to a paper (kind paper, the default; library MyPaperLean, Mathlib) in ./my-paper-lean and git init it; its coverage.yaml waits for the paper's title and rows, then `formalization anchor`.

```bash
lean-pkg new my-paper-lean
```

Sample output:

```text
created my-paper-lean/: package my-paper-lean (kind paper), library MyPaperLean, v4.35.0-rc2, Mathlib v4.35.0-rc2; 15 files, git initialized, nothing committed, no registry read or written
```

Scaffold a library (its coverage.yaml lists the example as the main result); the quickstart takes it from there.

```bash
lean-pkg new my-proof --kind library
```

The same in core Lean, with the author and the license named.

```bash
lean-pkg new my-proof --kind library --no-mathlib --author "Ada Lovelace" --license MIT
```
